Subject: Lead capture for FloorFootprint booth — badge scanning & consent

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking this on. We're running a two-day conference in Berlin (June 9-10) and need a simple, compliant lead-capture setup at our sponsor booth. Key asks:

- Badge scanner that can work offline and sync when the device sees internet.
- Field mapping to HubSpot (we use company-level and contact-level records).
- Explicit opt-in language for marketing for EU attendees (GDPR requirement).
- Retention window: we typically request 90 days of staging data before purge, but we can be flexible.

We have some specific badge types (attendee, exhibitor, press) and a QR fallback for badges that fail to scan. 

Can Redwood handle: offline capture, dedupe by email or badge id, and send a quick consent flag into HubSpot? Also: do you have recommended text we should display on the device (English + German)?

I'll loop in our ops alias if needed. Attached is a quick CSV of the badge schema.

Thanks,
Marta

FloorFootprint Events

Folks — technical notes and recommended mapping: 

- Scanner: firmware v2.1 (we'll ship devices preloaded). Works offline, AES-256 local store, auto-sync.
- Primary dedupe key: email if present, else badge_id. We also persist raw_scan_event for audit.
- HubSpot mapping (recommended):
  - contact.email -> contact.email
  - contact.first_name -> contact.firstname
  - contact.last_name -> contact.lastname
  - company.name -> company.name
  - properties.redwood_badge_type -> contact.redwood_badge_type (enumerated: attendee/exhibitor/press)
  - properties.redwood_consent_opt_in -> contact.redwood_consent_opt_in (boolean)
  - properties.redwood_scan_ts -> contact.redwood_scan_ts (ISO)

- Retention: we'll stage in our encrypted bucket for 90 days by default, then purge unless you request longer. We can expose an export link for your legal team.
- Offline handshake: device will emit signed manifest of scan batches; server validates signature before ingest.
- Dedupe caveat: if two records share no email, we won't auto-merge company records; we'll create separate contacts and surface potential duplicates in HubSpot.

Action items:
1) Marta: confirm the exact HubSpot property internal names or we map to the names above.
2) Marta: provide the EU consent text in English + German. We'll display that verbatim on the scanner UI and capture a boolean.
3) Dylan: schedule device provisioning window (we need 48 hours on-site to QA).

Ben
Senior Field Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick update: venue is in Berlin (so GDPR applies). Below is the consent language our legal team approved (English + German). Please use exactly these strings on the device and push a boolean flag into HubSpot when an attendee taps OK.

English: "I consent to FloorFootprint Events and its partners contacting me by email about products and services. I understand my data will be processed in accordance with the privacy policy: https://floorfootprint.com/privacy."

German: "Ich stimme zu, dass mich FloorFootprint Events und seine Partner per E-Mail über Produkte und Dienstleistungen informieren. Ich verstehe, dass meine Daten gemäß der Datenschutzrichtlinie verarbeitet werden: https://floorfootprint.com/datenschutz."

We also need to handle data subject requests: if an attendee asks to be deleted after the show, please provide the process and timing — we need to be able to confirm within 30 days.

Attachment: floorfootprint_consent_v2.docx (stub)

One more ask: can you provide a small banner (320x100) for the scanner UI in German? Our ops team will send finalized assets.

Best,
Marta
